beats.caption: A swarm of {agents} agents trades inside three human-signed envelopes. Each gauge is the day's budget, shared by every agent that draws on it.
beats.title: Calm

beats.caption: Same run, now with the arena's labels revealed. Red dots are bad orders. With nothing in front of them, every one reaches the exchange: {attack_usd} of bad orders reached the gate in this run.
beats.title: The attack starts

beats.caption: Rewind to the first attack and replay it with the verdicts. The mandate gate refuses or holds {gate_blocked_share} of bad dollars. The rest fit the envelope and pass it: the order-risk layer is what stops those.
beats.title: The guard

beats.caption: Held orders go to a person, ordered by expected bad dollars. Jev's advice is shown as advice only: it can raise an order in the queue, never approve or release one.
beats.title: The human

beats.caption: Every figure here comes from a committed result file, linked beside it. The caveats sit next to the numbers they qualify.
beats.title: The proof

focus.title: Five agents, one position

limits: Agents, fills and labels are simulated: the arena's labels are ground truth the guard never sees.

The mandate gate's decisions are the recorded ones. The order-risk layer is replayed over those decisions point in time; budget a stopped colluder would have freed for honest agents is not re-simulated.
The order-risk model never trained on seed 7. The Jev advice is replayed from recordings; it is advice, and code decides.
The recording's hash chain is an index of the stream file, not the L8 receiver's ledger. The receiver's agreement and its revocation behaviour come from separate runs and are labelled as such.
